SL-008 is implemented and committed as `aad2f9a`. `npm test` passes all 25 tests and `npm run typecheck` is clean. I wrote the tests first and ran them. Eight of the new ones failed, and the remaining ones passed already. Then I made the changes: - **`src/tasks.ts`:** `listTasks` now orders by `created_at DESC, id DESC`. Before, it used `ORDER BY id`. The `id` tiebreak puts the task saved last first when two tasks share the same instant. - **`public/index.html`:** I added a `

` message above the task list. - **`public/app.js`:** `showTasks` now sets `emptyState.hidden = tasks.length > 0`, so the message shows only when there are no tasks. The new tests are in `tests/list-order.test.ts`: - **AC-1:** Posting A, B, C returns C, B, A. A second test checks that creation time decides the order, not the id. - **AC-2:** Tasks inserted with an identical `created_at` come back last-saved-first on 20 repeated reads. A second test posts 30 tasks back to back and checks they come back in reverse. - **AC-3:** The page has the `empty-state` element outside the list. I ran `public/app.js` against a fake page to check the message is visible with no tasks and hidden with tasks. An empty database also answers 200 with no tasks. - **AC-4:** I seeded 1000 tasks and made 20 sequential `GET /api/tasks` requests. The test requires p95 under 100 ms and a body under 400,000 bytes, and it passes. There are no changes to the database layer, no new endpoint and no new field, as the slice requires. I did not run Stryker mutation testing. The empty-state check runs the script against a fake page, not a real browser.
